title: Every Real Singleton Is Meagre
content: isMeagre_singleton_real shows {x} ⊆ ℝ is meagre. A singleton is closed (T1), and interior {x} = ∅ because ℝ has no isolated points (interior_singleton, which needs NeBot (𝓝[≠] x) — available since ℝ is a PerfectSpace). By IsClosed.isNowhereDense_iff the singleton is nowhere dense, and a nowhere-dense set is meagre (IsNowhereDense.isMeagre).
mathContext: $\overline{\{x\}} = \{x\}$ and $\operatorname{int}\{x\} = \varnothing$, so $\{x\}$ is nowhere dense, hence meagre.

title: ℚ Is Meagre in ℝ
content: isMeagre_rationals writes the rationals as the countable union ⋃ q : ℚ, {(q : ℝ)} (Set.iUnion_singleton_eq_range applied to the cast ℚ → ℝ) and concludes meagreness from isMeagre_iUnion, since each singleton is meagre. This is the 'small' half of the meagre/dense clash that obstructs ℚ from being a Gδ.
mathContext: $\mathbb{Q} = \bigcup_{q \in \mathbb{Q}} \{q\}$ is a countable union of nowhere-dense singletons, hence meagre.

title: The Rationals Are Not a Gδ Set
content: not_isGδ_rationals: if ℚ were a Gδ, then being dense (dense_rationals := Rat.denseRange_cast) it would be residual and therefore not meagre (not_isMeagre_of_isGδ_of_dense, valid because ℝ is a Baire space). But ℚ is meagre — contradiction. This is the Baire-category obstruction reused from the parent entry's meagre/residual dichotomy.
mathContext: Dense $G_\delta$ $\Rightarrow$ residual $\Rightarrow$ non-meagre; but $\mathbb{Q}$ is meagre, so $\mathbb{Q}$ is not $G_\delta$.

title: Capstone: No Continuity Set Equals ℚ
content: continuitySet_ne_rationals: for every f : ℝ → ℝ the set {x | ContinuousAt f x} is a Gδ (Mathlib's IsGδ.setOf_continuousAt), so it cannot equal the non-Gδ set ℚ. Rewriting along an assumed equality turns the deep fact into a one-line contradiction with not_isGδ_rationals. This is the classical impossibility theorem discussed alongside Thomae's function.
mathContext: $\{x : \operatorname{ContinuousAt} f\,x\}$ is always $G_\delta$; $\mathbb{Q}$ is not; hence they are never equal.

title: No Function Continuous Exactly at the Rationals
content: no_function_continuous_exactly_at_rationals is the 'no such function' restatement: there is no f : ℝ → ℝ with ContinuousAt f x ↔ ¬ Irrational x (i.e. continuous at every rational, discontinuous at every irrational). The hypothesis would make the continuity set equal to ℚ = {x | ¬ Irrational x}, contradicting continuitySet_ne_rationals.

title: The One-Sided Asymmetry
content: irrationals_isGδ_no_obstruction pairs IsGδ.setOf_irrational (the irrationals ARE a Gδ) with not_isGδ_setOf_not_irrational (the rationals are not). The Gδ property splits the two sides of ℝ asymmetrically: the impossibility theorem applies only to the rational side, and Thomae's function (continuous exactly at the irrationals) shows the irrational side is genuinely realisable.
mathContext: Irrationals: $G_\delta$ (realisable as a continuity set). Rationals: not $G_\delta$ (impossible).
